body.statement: The functional \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) is nonnegative and symmetric, is unchanged when either encoder is relabeled by a node permutation and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms, vanishes on every such common quotient class, and obeys the quotient triangle inequality. Moreover, on the bounded-density and bi-Lipschitz class it is uniformly equivalent to either directed aligned \(L^2\) loss, so replacing the reference model by its competitor cannot change a modulus exponent.
body.justification: A law-to-representation modulus and a confidence-set diameter require an order-free quotient geometry rather than a loss directed from one selected model.
body.gap: The exact-identification papers specify an equivalence class but do not metrize approximate encoder recovery under two competing observed laws.
body.consumer: Every lower bound, upper modulus, estimator guarantee, and confidence-set diameter uses the same symmetric quotient object.
